title: Decision gate: what must be answered before a decision is reasonable

rows.question: What is the stake unit and total bankroll the leaderboard measures?
rows.why_it_matters: Every stake rule (flat, Kelly, fractional Kelly) needs a bankroll; without it ROI and drawdown cannot be compared across strategies.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing. No bankroll figure has been supplied.
rows.information_missing: Stake unit, bankroll size, max exposure per slate.
rows.how_to_get_it: Owner decision recorded in the repo; no external source exists.
rows.blocks_decision: Staking rules, reward rules, leaderboard scoring

rows.question: Which price feed will supply market spreads, totals and player-prop prices?
rows.why_it_matters: Originating our own lines is only meaningful against a market price; without it we cannot measure closing line value.
rows.information_we_have: No official NFL or club source publishes betting prices (verified: nfl.com and club sites publish none).
rows.information_missing: A licensed/account feed for opening and closing prices.
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide a feed (owner's sportsbook account export, or a licensed data vendor) and record it here.
rows.blocks_decision: Originating lines, CLV gate, parlay pricing, prop pricing

rows.question: Do we record the price at the time we originate the line, at close, or both?
rows.why_it_matters: CLV is measured against the closing number; without a timestamp convention the gate is undefined.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: Timestamp convention and storage format for price snapshots.
rows.how_to_get_it: Define in the data schema; needs the feed from Q-02 first.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: What is the official source for final scores and box scores?
rows.why_it_matters: Every backtest, ROI figure and skill test needs verified results.
rows.information_we_have: nfl.com/schedules and nfl.com/scores return no server-rendered results table (verified by probe).
rows.information_missing: A results source that can be cited.
rows.how_to_get_it: Probe candidate official endpoints further, or license a feed; meanwhile no results table is published.

rows.question: Is this paper (simulated) only, or will real money be staked?
rows.why_it_matters: Changes the compliance, logging and reward requirements entirely.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing stated.
rows.information_missing: A yes/no scope decision, plus any jurisdiction constraints.
rows.how_to_get_it: Owner decision recorded in the repo.

rows.question: How are rewards for top strategies defined, funded and paid?
rows.why_it_matters: The brief requires rewards for top performing strategies; nobody can build a reward without the rule.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: Reward structure, funding source, eligibility, settlement period.
rows.how_to_get_it: Owner decision; a reward rule document committed to the repo.

rows.question: What is the minimum number of graded bets before a strategy is allowed to bet real size?
rows.why_it_matters: This is the single strongest defence against a lucky run being mistaken for skill.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: A minimum bet count, expressed per market type.
rows.how_to_get_it: Set from the validation gate design; needs the results feed from Q-04 to calibrate.

rows.question: Which statistical test decides that a result is skill and not luck?
rows.why_it_matters: The brief explicitly asks to remove luck from the equation.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing decided.
rows.information_missing: Chosen test, significance level, and how multiple strategies are corrected for.
rows.how_to_get_it: Choose and record: binomial/CLT test on hit rate vs the break-even probability implied by the price, plus a t-test on CLV.

rows.question: How do we correct for the fact that many strategies are tested at once?
rows.why_it_matters: With a leaderboard, the best-looking strategy is often the luckiest; uncorrected thresholds guarantee false positives.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: Correction method (Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg) and a cap on the number of live strategies.
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide in the gate design; document in the methodology page.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: What correlation threshold makes two legs ineligible for the same parlay?
rows.why_it_matters: Correlated legs are the main way a parlay quietly multiplies risk.
rows.information_we_have: Correlation values computable from official season team stats (n=32) only; see the Correlations page.
rows.information_missing: Play-by-play or game-level data for true same-game correlations.
rows.how_to_get_it: Compute team-level correlations now from official data (done); add game-level later once a results feed exists.

rows.question: Are player-prop correlations in scope, and from what data?
rows.why_it_matters: Player-prop combos are in the brief, but no official source publishes prop-level data.
rows.information_we_have: No official source for player prop lines or player prop results was found.
rows.information_missing: A source for player-level usage and results.
rows.how_to_get_it: Probe official player-stats pages; if unavailable, flag and leave blank.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: Which injury designation should trigger an automatic line move?
rows.why_it_matters: The league publishes three practice levels and three game statuses; each carries different information.
rows.information_we_have: Official definitions of the designations (nfl.com competition-committee release).
rows.information_missing: Historical hit rates for each designation — needs the results feed from Q-04.
rows.how_to_get_it: Compute once a results feed exists; until then the deficiency watch flags but does not price.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: How do we treat a player who is Questionable but a full participant on the final report?
rows.why_it_matters: Official policy says a certain player is removed from the game status report; a listed player is genuinely uncertain.
rows.information_we_have: The league's own definition of Questionable and Full Participation.
rows.information_missing: Empirical play rates by designation — needs results data.
rows.how_to_get_it: Defer to Q-12.

rows.question: When the official report changes after we publish a line, do we re-originate?
rows.why_it_matters: Reports are updated through the week; a stale line is worse than no line.
rows.information_we_have: The refresh job re-pulls the official injury report every 6 hours.
rows.information_missing: A re-pricing policy and a versioned line history.
rows.how_to_get_it: Define the policy; the pipeline already timestamps every pull.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: Which clubs' official depth charts are authoritative when a club site is unreachable?
rows.why_it_matters: The deficiency model depends on depth charts; some club sites currently fail to return a parsable page.
rows.information_we_have: Per-club attempt log with HTTP status and page title (see Depth Charts page).
rows.information_missing: A fallback official source, or acceptance that those clubs are uncovered.
rows.how_to_get_it: Already handled by flagging: uncovered clubs are published on Flagged for Review, never guessed.

rows.question: How deep must a club's chart be printed before we call a position 'covered'?
rows.why_it_matters: A position with only one name printed leaves no verified replacement.
rows.information_we_have: The number of names printed per position is in the depth chart dataset.
rows.information_missing: A coverage rule.
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide: require at least two printed names to call a slot covered.

rows.question: Are practice-squad elevations and roster transactions in scope for the deficiency model?
rows.why_it_matters: A replacement can come from outside the printed depth chart.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing verified.
rows.information_missing: An official transactions source that is machine-readable.
rows.how_to_get_it: Probe official transaction pages; if unavailable, flag.

rows.question: Do we need venue and weather data, and is there an official source?
rows.why_it_matters: Totals and kicking props are weather sensitive.
rows.information_we_have: No official NFL weather source was verified.
rows.information_missing: An official or licensed weather feed.
rows.how_to_get_it: Only adopt if a citable source is found; otherwise leave the field blank.

rows.question: Do we need referee assignments and their tendencies?
rows.why_it_matters: Penalty-rate tendencies are a real totals and side signal.
rows.information_we_have: No official, machine-readable officials assignment source was verified.
rows.information_missing: A citable source.
rows.how_to_get_it: Leave out until a source is verified.

rows._source_label: Official page cited in this row
rows.question: Do we need rest days and travel distance?
rows.why_it_matters: Short weeks and long travel are standard NFL model inputs.
rows.information_we_have: Schedule pages exist but are client-rendered, so no verified table was extracted.
rows.information_missing: A citable source for game times and venues.
rows.how_to_get_it: Probe further; otherwise leave blank and flag.

rows.question: Do we need play-by-play or drive-level data?
rows.why_it_matters: Success rate, pace and play-type splits are the backbone of modern NFL models.
rows.information_we_have: No official static play-by-play source was verified.
rows.information_missing: A licensed play-by-play feed, or official gamebooks in a machine-readable form.
rows.how_to_get_it: Probe official gamebook endpoints; if unavailable, flag as a known model limitation.

rows.question: Which markets do we originate first: side, total, or moneyline?
rows.why_it_matters: Each needs different inputs and different validation.
rows.information_we_have: Official team stats and standings support a side and total model today.
rows.information_missing: A prioritisation decision.
rows.how_to_get_it: Recommend side first, then total (see Suggestions S-04).

rows.question: What is the definition of a 'useful signal'?
rows.why_it_matters: The brief asks for useful signals without defining usefulness.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: A measurable definition (e.g. positive expected value after vig at a stated confidence).
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide and record in the methodology page.

rows.question: Are parlays built from our own correlations only, or also from market-implied correlation?
rows.why_it_matters: Sportsbooks price same-game parlays with their own correlation assumptions; beating that needs a view.
rows.information_we_have: Our own team-level correlations from official stats.
rows.information_missing: Market-implied correlation — needs the price feed from Q-02.
rows.how_to_get_it: Defer to Q-02.

rows.question: Who approves a suggestion and who can change a gate threshold?
rows.why_it_matters: The brief wants a review step before implementation; it does not name a reviewer.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: Named decision owner and a recorded decision for each suggestion.
rows.how_to_get_it: Owner decision recorded in the Suggestions table (decision_status column).

rows.question: What happens to a strategy that passes gates on paper but loses live?
rows.why_it_matters: Paper validation never fully protects against live slippage.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: A demotion rule (drawdown or CLV threshold that sends a strategy back to paper).
rows.how_to_get_it: Define in the gate set; needs Q-07 first.

rows.question: How are leaderboard ties broken?
rows.why_it_matters: A leaderboard needs a deterministic ordering.
rows.information_we_have: Nothing.
rows.information_missing: Tie-break rule (e.g. more graded bets wins, then earlier registration).
rows.how_to_get_it: Decide and record on the Strategy Lab page.

rows.question: How long are data snapshots retained?
rows.why_it_matters: Correlations and CLV need history; unbounded storage is a cost.
rows.information_we_have: The refresh job commits each pull to git, so history exists by default.
rows.information_missing: A retention rule.
rows.how_to_get_it: Git history is the archive; decide whether to prune.

rows.question: What is the recovery path if a scheduled refresh fails for several cycles?
rows.why_it_matters: Stale injury data would silently degrade the model.
rows.information_we_have: The refresh job records a run report and never overwrites good data with an empty pull.
rows.information_missing: An alerting rule.
rows.how_to_get_it: Add a job that fails loudly when a dataset returns zero rows for N consecutive runs.

rows.question: What is the branch naming rule when this harness pins a session to one branch?
rows.why_it_matters: The brief asks for session-<id>/<task> branches; the harness requires all work on the current branch.
rows.information_we_have: Both instructions, quoted in the brief and in the session rules.
rows.information_missing: A resolution from the owner, or an accepted deviation.
rows.how_to_get_it: Logged as irregularity F-01 on the Flagged for Review page; the task board records the single-branch scope.
